issues.description: Method GroverMultiQubitWithAuxiliaryQubit.simulate: the template declares the return type as list[complex] (a statevector) while the problem statement (Exercise 2.6) and the reference solution expect and return measurement counts (dict[str, int]). This mismatch appears in the template file but the intended behavior documented in the exercise and implemented in the solution is to run the circuit on a simulator (after reversing bits) and return a histogram of measurement counts. The inconsistency can confuse students about whether to return a statevector or measurement counts and may cause type-related test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature and docstring for GroverMultiQubitWithAuxiliaryQubit.simulate to match the exercise and solution: change the return annotation from list[complex] to dict[str, int] (or typing.Dict[str,int]) and update the docstring to state that the method should reverse bits (qc = qc.reverse_bits()) as needed, run the circuit on a simulator, and return measurement counts. Example change: def simulate(self, qc: QuantumCircuit) -> dict[str, int]: and ensure the implementation performs qc = qc.reverse_bits(); execute on a Qiskit simulator; return result.get_counts(qc). This aligns the template with the Problem Statement (Exercise 2.6) and the provided solution.
